issues.editorial: Our inaugural issue collects the first peer-reviewed work by Synthica's student researchers.
Closing our first volume with work spanning computational biology and behavioural economics.

articles.title: Modeling Coral Bleaching Thresholds Under Regional Warming Scenarios
articles.abstract: Coral reefs face escalating thermal stress. Using public NOAA reef temperature datasets, we model bleaching onset thresholds across three regional warming scenarios and estimate recovery windows. Our results suggest that fortnightly thermal anomaly exposure is a stronger predictor of bleaching onset than seasonal means, with implications for local monitoring programs run by student research teams.
references: Hughes, T. P. et al. Global warming and recurrent mass bleaching of corals. Nature 543, 373-377 (2017).
NOAA Coral Reef Watch. Daily 5km Satellite Coral Bleaching Heat Stress Monitoring (2024).
Sully, S. et al. A global analysis of coral bleaching over the past two decades. Nat. Commun. 10, 1264 (2019).

articles.title: A Lightweight CNN for Classifying Pollinator Species from Smartphone Images
articles.abstract: Citizen-science pollinator surveys are limited by identification skill. We train a lightweight convolutional neural network on 12,000 smartphone images to classify six common pollinator families with 91% accuracy on held-out data, small enough to run offline on mid-range phones. We release the model and a labelling protocol suitable for classroom deployments.
references: Howard, A. G. et al. MobileNets: Efficient convolutional neural networks for mobile vision applications. arXiv:1704.04861 (2017).
Van Horn, G. et al. The iNaturalist species classification and detection dataset. CVPR (2018).

articles.title: Do Deadlines Help? A Field Experiment on Task Completion in Student Research Teams
articles.abstract: We randomize soft versus hard deadlines across 40 student research teams and measure task completion over eight weeks. Hard deadlines increase on-time completion by 23 percentage points but reduce self-reported work quality; soft deadlines with visible peer progress achieve comparable completion without the quality penalty.
references: Ariely, D. & Wertenbroch, K. Procrastination, deadlines, and performance. Psychol. Sci. 13, 219-224 (2002).

articles.title: Synthesis and Characterisation of Biodegradable Chitosan Films from Shrimp Shell Waste
articles.abstract: We extract chitosan from local shrimp shell waste and cast films plasticised with glycerol, characterising tensile strength, water vapour permeability, and biodegradation over 30 days of soil burial. Films with 25% glycerol balance flexibility and degradation, suggesting a viable classroom-scale route from food waste to packaging prototypes.
references: Rinaudo, M. Chitin and chitosan: Properties and applications. Prog. Polym. Sci. 31, 603-632 (2006).

articles.title: Backyard Pollinator Diversity Across Urban Garden Microhabitats: A Season-Long Census
articles.abstract: Weekly fifteen-minute pollinator counts at six urban garden sites over one growing season reveal that native bee diversity tracks flowering plant cover more closely than site area. We provide a reproducible census protocol and discuss implications for school-garden biodiversity programs.
references: Baldock, K. C. R. et al. A systems approach reveals urban pollinator hotspots and conservation opportunities. Nat. Ecol. Evol. 3, 363-373 (2019).

articles.title: Estimating Exoplanet Transit Depths with a Backyard 8-inch Telescope: Limits and Best Practice
articles.abstract: Using 42 nights of photometry from a consumer 8-inch reflector, we quantify the practical detection floor for exoplanet transit depths in suburban skies. Careful differential photometry recovers transits of 1.2% depth with 3-sigma confidence; we publish an open reduction pipeline tuned for student observatories.
references: Collins, K. A. et al. AstroImageJ: Image processing and photometric extraction for ultra-precise astronomical light curves. Astron. J. 153, 77 (2017).
